external:enums/match-type.json.description: Keyword targeting match type. broad: ads may serve on queries semantically related to the keyword. phrase: ads serve when the query contains the keyword phrase. exact: ads serve only when the query matches the keyword exactly.

enumDescriptions.broad: Ads may serve on queries semantically related to the keyword
enumDescriptions.phrase: Ads serve when the query contains the keyword phrase in order
enumDescriptions.exact: Ads serve only when the query matches the keyword exactly

external:core/targeting-overlay-requirem.title: Targeting Overlay Requirements
external:core/targeting-overlay-requirem.description: Buyer minimum requirements for targeting dimensions that will be selected on packages later. This request shape deliberately excludes seller limits such as max_values_per_package and max_packages. Matching is capability containment: where a field permits a boolean form, a requirement value of true matches product support true or any valid positive support object, and product support true satisfies every protocol-valid structured requirement. Otherwise, structured product support must contain the structured requirement. For geo_regions and geo_regions_exclude, every requested country must exist; requested all_values requires supported all_values; and requested values must be a subset of supported values unless support declares all_values. For geo_places and geo_places_exclude, every requested system and country key must exist and each requested place-type and system-version array must be a subset of the corresponding product array. Include and exclude fields match independently. Every valid structured requirement or support object represents a positive capability; empty, extension-only, and false-only objects are invalid. Object fields the buyer did not request do not participate. Missing or unknown required fields do not match. Numeric seller limits are disclosed only in Product.overlay_support and never participate in matching.

anyOf.description: Require later package-level selection for the listed canonical browser families. The requirement matches unrestricted true support or structured support containing every requested family.

external:core/geo-region-requirement.jso.title: Geographic Region Requirement
external:core/geo-region-requirement.jso.description: Buyer minimum requirements for ISO 3166-2 subdivision values that must remain independently selectable later. Country keys prevent a false cross-country capability claim. all_values requires support for every protocol-valid ISO subdivision active in the seller's support snapshot when the declaration is issued; values requests an exact finite candidate set. Exact delivery values known now belong in get_products.targeting_overlay instead.

countries.description: Required ISO subdivision support keyed by ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country.

all_values.description: Require every protocol-valid ISO 3166-2 subdivision active in the seller's returned support snapshot for this country to remain selectable.

values.description: Exact finite set of ISO 3166-2 identifiers the buyer may select later.

external:core/geo-place-requirement.json.title: Geographic Place Requirement
external:core/geo-place-requirement.json.description: Identifier systems and collision-safe country/type pairs the buyer must be allowed to select later.

catalogRequirement.description: Required country/type pairs and optional exact catalog versions for one identifier system. Country keys prevent a false Cartesian product between countries and place types.

system_versions.description: Optional exact catalog versions that must remain selectable. Versions are opaque strings, not ordered ranges.

external:core/positive-postal-area-suppo.title: Positive Postal Area Support
external:core/positive-postal-area-suppo.description: Non-vacuous postal capability used for hard targeting requirements and product overlay support. At least one native system array or true-valued deprecated alias is required. The general seller-capabilities postal schema remains permissive for backward compatibility, but an empty or false-only map cannot satisfy a hard discovery requirement.

external:core/postal-area-support.json.title: Postal Area Support
external:core/postal-area-support.json.description: Declares supported postal area systems. Native support is keyed by ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country with arrays of country-local postal systems. Deprecated country-fused boolean aliases may be included during migration.

external:media-buy/outcome-target.json.title: Outcome Target
external:media-buy/outcome-target.json.description: Reverse-forecast planning input: the buyer states the outcome needed and the seller solves for budget. The goal is a compact planning-time object — delivery metrics use the same forecastable-metric vocabulary as forecast points, and outcome events use the same event-type vocabulary — so every permitted goal has a defined answer: the seller responds with total_budget_guidance on proposals and forecasts whose points carry the goal's metric or event key in metrics, using forecast_range_unit 'clicks' or 'conversions' to structure the curve where those units apply. Execution machinery (targets, priorities, event sources, vendor bindings) belongs to the package-level optimization-goal, which shares this vocabulary; buyers carry the same metric or event name from plan to buy. A planning input, not a delivery guarantee — obligations arise only at proposal finalization. Sellers not declaring media_buy.outcome_target MUST reject the field with UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE rather than silently ignore it; declaring sellers MAY reject a goal they cannot plan against (for example 'spend', which restates budget) with INVALID_REQUEST naming criteria.outcome_target.goal.

goal.description: The outcome to plan against: a seller-tracked delivery metric or an advertiser conversion event.

oneOf.description: Plan against a seller-tracked delivery metric. The response forecast carries this metric as a key in points' metrics.

metric.description: Delivery metric to plan for, in the same vocabulary forecast points report.

oneOf.description: Plan against an advertiser conversion event. The response forecast carries this event type as a key in points' metrics.

event_type.description: Conversion event to plan for, in the same vocabulary forecast points report.

custom_event_name.description: Required when event_type is 'custom'. Platform-specific name for the custom event.

volume.description: Desired total volume of the goal's metric or event across the planned flight.

external:enums/forecastable-metric.json.title: Forecastable Metric
external:enums/forecastable-metric.json.description: Standard delivery, engagement, and availability metric names for forecasts. **Most values mirror `available-metric.json`** (the canonical closed delivery vocabulary) — `impressions`, `clicks`, `spend`, `views`, `completed_views`, `engagements`, `follows`, `saves`, `profile_visits`, `downloads`, `plays`, `reach`, `frequency`, `grps` are all shared. **Forecast-only deltas** are `audience_size`, `measured_impressions`, and `coverage_rate` — these exist here because forecasts can reasonably project them but delivery reporting today does not surface them as `available-metric` entries (delivery uses other paths: e.g., `measured_impressions` flows through `vendor_metric_values` when a third-party vendor reports it). When the industry converges on adding any of these to delivery reporting, those values graduate into `available-metric.json` and this enum's deltas shrink. For outcome/conversion forecasts (purchases, leads, app installs, etc.), use event-type enum values as metric keys instead. The ForecastPoint metrics map accepts any string key, so both forecastable-metric and event-type values can be used together.

enumDescriptions.reach: Estimated unique reach. The reach_unit field on DeliveryForecast specifies the measurement unit (individuals, households, devices, etc.).
enumDescriptions.impressions: Estimated ad-server or first-party delivery count. When measured_impressions is also present, impressions represents the seller's own delivery count while measured_impressions represents the third-party currency count — both may appear on the same forecast point as complementary layers.
enumDescriptions.spend: Estimated spend in the forecast currency
enumDescriptions.completed_views: Estimated video/audio completions. Threshold depends on view_duration_seconds if set on the optimization goal.
enumDescriptions.grps: Estimated Gross Rating Points (for CPP). When present, the demographic_system and demographic fields on DeliveryForecast should specify the target demographic.
enumDescriptions.engagements: Estimated engagements (social reactions, comments, shares, story opens, overlay taps, etc.)
enumDescriptions.follows: Estimated new followers, page likes, or free channel/feed subscribes
enumDescriptions.saves: Estimated saves, bookmarks, playlist adds, or pins
enumDescriptions.profile_visits: Estimated visits to the brand's in-platform page or profile
enumDescriptions.measured_impressions: Impressions as counted by the third-party measurement provider specified in measurement_source on DeliveryForecast. Complementary to impressions — both may appear on the same forecast point. impressions is the ad-server delivery count; measured_impressions is the third-party currency count. Present when measurement_source is set. Use with method 'guaranteed' for contractually committed delivery, or with method 'modeled' for third-party-measured estimates without a guarantee.
enumDescriptions.downloads: Estimated downloads. Primary currency for podcast advertising per IAB Podcast Measurement guidelines.
enumDescriptions.plays: Number of times the ad creative is displayed on a DOOH screen or played in a loop. Raw play count before any impression multiplier is applied. Use alongside impressions or measured_impressions when buyers need both the play count and the multiplied audience figure.
enumDescriptions.coverage_rate: Share of the declared forecast scope represented by this point. Used primarily for signal coverage and availability breakdowns. Range 0.0 to 1.0.

external:enums/event-type.json.title: Event Type
external:enums/event-type.json.description: Standard marketing event types for event logging, aligned with IAB ECAPI

enumDescriptions.view_content: User viewed specific content (product, article, etc.)
enumDescriptions.select_content: User selected or clicked on content (article, video, etc.)
enumDescriptions.select_item: User selected a specific product or item from a list
enumDescriptions.share: User shared content via social or messaging
enumDescriptions.add_to_cart: User added an item to cart
enumDescriptions.remove_from_cart: User removed an item from cart
enumDescriptions.add_to_wishlist: User added an item to a wishlist
enumDescriptions.refund: A purchase was fully or partially refunded (adjusts ROAS)
enumDescriptions.lead: User expressed interest (form submission, signup, etc.)
enumDescriptions.qualify_lead: Lead qualified by sales or scoring criteria
enumDescriptions.close_convert_lead: Lead converted to a customer or closed deal
enumDescriptions.disqualify_lead: Lead disqualified or marked as not viable
enumDescriptions.subscribe: User started a paid subscription or paid membership
enumDescriptions.follow: User made a free, durable opt-in to an account, channel, feed, list, podcast, or similar owned property
enumDescriptions.content_view: User meaningfully consumed a content unit, such as a watch, listen, stream, episode play, or read
enumDescriptions.watch_milestone: User reached a content progress threshold, such as 25%, 50%, 75%, 100%, or a seconds-viewed milestone
enumDescriptions.schedule: User scheduled an appointment or event
enumDescriptions.submit_application: User submitted an application (loan, job, etc.)

external:core/catalog-selection.json.title: Catalog Selection
external:core/catalog-selection.json.description: Reference and item selectors for a catalog already known to the seller. Feed URLs, mappings, schedules, and inline catalog data belong to sync_catalogs. Different selector fields combine with AND semantics; values within ids, gtins, or tags use OR semantics.

catalog_id.description: Seller-known catalog identifier returned by sync_catalogs.

external:core/catalog.json.title: Catalog
external:core/catalog.json.description: A typed data feed. Catalogs carry the items, locations, stock levels, or pricing that publishers use to render ads. They can be synced to a platform via sync_catalogs (managed lifecycle with approval), provided inline, or fetched from an external URL. The catalog type determines the item schema and can be structural (offering, product, inventory, store, promotion) or vertical-specific (hotel, flight, job, vehicle, real_estate, education, destination, app). Selectors (ids, tags, category, query) filter items regardless of sourcing method.

catalog_id.description: Buyer's identifier for this catalog. Required when syncing via sync_catalogs. When used in creatives, references a previously synced catalog on the account.

name.description: Human-readable name for this catalog (e.g., 'Summer Products 2025', 'Amsterdam Store Locations').

type.description: Catalog type. Structural types: 'offering' (AdCP Offering objects), 'product' (ecommerce entries), 'inventory' (stock per location), 'store' (physical locations), 'promotion' (deals and pricing). Vertical types: 'hotel', 'flight', 'job', 'vehicle', 'real_estate', 'education', 'destination', 'app' — each with an industry-specific item schema.

url.description: URL to an external catalog feed. The platform fetches and resolves items from this URL. For offering-type catalogs, the feed contains an array of Offering objects. For other types, the feed format is determined by feed_format. When omitted with type 'product', the platform uses its synced copy of the brand's product catalog.

feed_format.description: Format of the external feed at url. Required when url points to a non-AdCP feed (e.g., Google Merchant Center XML, Meta Product Catalog). Omit for offering-type catalogs where the feed is native AdCP JSON.

update_frequency.description: How often the platform should re-fetch the feed from url. Only applicable when url is provided. Platforms may use this as a hint for polling schedules.

items.description: Inline catalog data. The item schema depends on the catalog type: Offering objects for 'offering', StoreItem for 'store', HotelItem for 'hotel', FlightItem for 'flight', JobItem for 'job', VehicleItem for 'vehicle', RealEstateItem for 'real_estate', EducationItem for 'education', DestinationItem for 'destination', AppItem for 'app', or freeform objects for 'product', 'inventory', and 'promotion'. Mutually exclusive with url — provide one or the other, not both. Implementations should validate items against the type-specific schema.

ids.description: Filter catalog to exact canonical item keys. The key field is offering_id for offering, store_id for store, hotel_id for hotel, flight_id for flight, job_id for job, vehicle_id for vehicle, listing_id for real_estate, program_id for education, destination_id for destination, and app_id for app. Product, inventory, and promotion catalogs use the stable normalized source identifier retained during ingestion (for example a retailer SKU). The same canonical key is used by catalog availability item_id.

gtins.description: Filter product-type catalogs by GTIN identifiers for cross-retailer catalog matching. Accepts standard GTIN formats (GTIN-8, UPC-A/GTIN-12, EAN-13/GTIN-13, GTIN-14). Only applicable when type is 'product'.

tags.description: Filter catalog to items with these tags. Tags are matched using OR logic — items matching any tag are included.

category.description: Filter catalog to items in this category (e.g., 'beverages/soft-drinks', 'chef-positions').

query.description: Natural language filter for catalog items (e.g., 'all pasta sauces under $5', 'amsterdam vacancies').

conversion_events.description: Event types that represent conversions for items in this catalog. Declares what events the platform should attribute to catalog items — e.g., a job catalog converts via submit_application, a product catalog via purchase. The event's content_ids field carries the item IDs that connect back to catalog items. Use content_id_type to declare what identifier type content_ids values represent.

content_id_type.description: Identifier type that the event's content_ids field should be matched against for items in this catalog. For example, 'gtin' means content_ids values are Global Trade Item Numbers, 'sku' means retailer SKUs. Omit when using a custom identifier scheme not listed in the enum.

feed_field_mappings.description: Declarative normalization rules for external feeds. Maps non-standard feed field names, date formats, price encodings, and image URLs to the AdCP catalog item schema. Applied during sync_catalogs ingestion. Supports field renames, named transforms (date, divide, boolean, split), static literal injection, and assignment of image URLs to typed asset pools.

examples.description: Synced product catalog from Google Merchant Center
Inventory feed for store-level stock data
Reference to a previously synced catalog by ID
Product catalog with GTIN cross-retailer matching and attribution
Inline store catalog with catchment areas

external:enums/catalog-type.json.title: Catalog Type
external:enums/catalog-type.json.description: The type of catalog feed. Determines the item schema and how the platform resolves catalog items. Multiple catalog types can be synced to the same account and referenced together in creatives.

external:enums/feed-format.json.title: Feed Format
external:enums/feed-format.json.description: Catalog feed formats. Determines how the platform (seller) parses items from an external feed URL. Each named value is an externally-documented feed specification a seller parses natively without buyer-supplied feed_field_mappings; values are vendor spec names (proper nouns), not semantic categories. Use `custom` + feed_field_mappings for any feed whose shape is not one of the named formats.

enumDescriptions.google_merchant_center: Google Merchant Center / Google Shopping product data specification — the de-facto e-commerce product-feed lingua franca that the other named commerce formats derive from.
enumDescriptions.facebook_catalog: Meta (Facebook / Instagram) product catalog feed — a Google-Merchant-Center-derived dialect, the closest clone of the GMC field set.
enumDescriptions.tiktok_shop: TikTok Shop product catalog feed — a GMC-derived dialect with material deltas (sku_id as the primary identifier rather than id, and a first-class video_link) that a GMC parser keyed on id would mis-parse.
enumDescriptions.pinterest_catalog: Pinterest product catalog feed — a GMC-derived dialect with stricter serialization (composite-encoded price and shipping, a mandatory google_product_category, space-delimited availability enums) that a strict GMC parser would mis-handle.
enumDescriptions.openai_product_feed: OpenAI Commerce product feed for ChatGPT shopping — a GMC-derived dialect adding ChatGPT-specific eligibility flags (is_eligible_search / is_eligible_checkout / is_eligible_ads). Spec: https://developers.openai.com/commerce/specs/file-upload/products
enumDescriptions.custom: A feed whose shape is not one of the named formats above. The buyer MUST supply feed_field_mappings to normalize it to the AdCP catalog item schema.

external:enums/content-id-type.json.title: Content ID Type
external:enums/content-id-type.json.description: Identifier type used in content_ids on conversion events to match back to catalog items. Omit when the identifier type is custom or not listed here.

external:core/catalog-field-mapping.json.title: Catalog Field Mapping
external:core/catalog-field-mapping.json.description: Declares how a field in an external feed maps to the AdCP catalog item schema. Used in sync_catalogs feed_field_mappings to normalize non-AdCP feeds (Google Merchant Center, LinkedIn Jobs XML, hotel XML, etc.) to the standard catalog item schema without requiring the buyer to preprocess every feed. Multiple mappings can assemble a nested object via dot notation (e.g., separate mappings for price.amount and price.currency).

feed_field.description: Field name in the external feed record. Omit when injecting a static literal value (use the value property instead).

catalog_field.description: Target field on the catalog item schema, using dot notation for nested fields (e.g., 'name', 'price.amount', 'location.city'). Mutually exclusive with asset_group_id.

asset_group_id.description: Places the feed field value (a URL) into a typed asset pool on the catalog item's assets array. The value is wrapped as an image or video asset in a group with this ID. Use standard group IDs: 'images_landscape', 'images_vertical', 'images_square', 'logo', 'video'. Mutually exclusive with catalog_field.

value.description: Static literal value to inject into catalog_field for every item, regardless of what the feed contains. Mutually exclusive with feed_field. Useful for fields the feed omits (e.g., currency when price is always USD, or a constant category value).

transform.description: Named transform to apply to the feed field value before writing to the catalog schema. See transform-specific parameters (format, timezone, by, separator).

format.description: For transform 'date': the input date format string (e.g., 'YYYYMMDD', 'MM/DD/YYYY', 'DD-MM-YYYY'). Output is always ISO 8601 (e.g., '2025-03-01'). Uses Unicode date pattern tokens.

timezone.description: For transform 'date': the timezone of the input value. IANA timezone identifier (e.g., 'UTC', 'America/New_York', 'Europe/Amsterdam'). Defaults to UTC when omitted.

by.description: For transform 'divide': the divisor to apply (e.g., 100 to convert integer cents to decimal dollars).

separator.description: For transform 'split': the separator character or string to split on. Defaults to ','.

default.description: Fallback value to use when feed_field is absent, null, or empty. Applied after any transform would have been applied. Allows optional feed fields to have a guaranteed baseline value.

examples.description: Date format transform — YYYYMMDD to ISO 8601
Static literal injection — currency not in feed
Image URL assigned to typed asset pool
Vertical photo URL assigned to vertical pool

external:core/opportunity-context.json.title: Opportunity Context
external:core/opportunity-context.json.description: Buyer-supplied context for one planning cycle across proposal request, decline, and media-buy creation. The opaque opportunity_id is stable within the seller and account scope; sellers associate it with proposals without treating it as proposal identity.

opportunity_id.description: Opaque buyer-assigned identifier for this planning cycle, scoped to the seller and account.

intent.description: How seriously the buyer is evaluating supply in this cycle.

planning_horizon.description: Inclusive calendar range in which the buyer expects the campaign to run.

response_deadline.description: Deadline by which the buyer needs a seller response.

status.description: Whether the planning cycle remains open. On calls after initial creation, omission means no status update and MUST NOT reopen or close the opportunity implicitly, except that successful create_media_buy proposal execution explicitly infers accepted closure.

close_reason.description: Why the opportunity closed. Required when status is closed.

close_detail.description: Optional non-sensitive context about closure. MUST NOT identify a competitor or disclose confidential clearing terms.

external:core/date-range.json.title: Date Range
external:core/date-range.json.description: A date range with inclusive start and end dates (ISO 8601 calendar dates). Used for billing periods, flight dates, and other calendar-day boundaries.
